mainTopic: Immersing the knife but not the cleaver; whether the חגיגה overrides שבת (בן דורתאי vs. the רבנן); and שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question from the previous amud: why would someone immerse his סכין on the 13th of ניסן but not his קופיץ, which is needed only for the חגיגה? The גמרא tries three cases: the פסח meat was plentiful, the פסח was brought בטומאה, and the נשיא died. Each one fails because nobody could know it in advance. The final answer is that the נשיא was a גוסס on the 13th. The knife then involves one doubt, so it is immersed, while the cleaver involves two doubts, so it is not. Next, a ברייתא tells of יהודה בן דורתאי, who broke away from the חכמים because he held that the חגיגה overrides שבת. רב finds his source in 'צאן ובקר', but רב אשי refuses to explain the view of those who broke away, and reads the פסוק as teaching that a מותר הפסח is brought as שלמים. The גמרא then asks why the רבנן do not let the חגיגה override שבת. רבי אילעא answers from 'seven days' in the פסוק about סוכות, and אביי defends this proof against רבין's challenge. Finally, עולא quotes רבי אלעזר that שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב count for neither שמחה nor חגיגה, and the source for this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Paschal meat was plentiful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case involves a קרבן פסח with plenty of meat, so no חגיגה is needed and no cleaver is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is one where the פסח is large (each person gets plenty of meat).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to why the cleaver was not immersed: there was enough פסח meat, so no חגיגה would be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חגיגה is brought together with the פסח only when the פסח meat is not enough to fill everyone up. If the meat is plentiful, there is no חגיגה. Since the cleaver is used only for the חגיגה, it would not be needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Large or plentiful. Here: the פסח has enough meat for everyone registered.
The festival peace-offering brought alongside the פסח when the פסח meat is not enough.
A cleaver, used to chop bones. It is not used on the פסח, whose bones may not be broken.

steps.confusionAlert: This answer responds to a question asked on the previous amud: why was the cleaver not immersed? Keep that question in mind through step 8, where it is finally resolved.

phrases.english: With a large (plentiful) Paschal offering.
phrases.notes: A one-word answer: few people registered, so there is plenty of meat and no חגיגה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question (on the previous amud) of why the cleaver was not immersed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One would expect the cleaver to be immersed too, in case a חגיגה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the פסח is plentiful, no חגיגה is brought, so there is no need for the cleaver.

steps.title: How would they know in advance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: on the 13th, how could anyone know the פסח will turn out to be plentiful?
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they know (already on the 13th)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first answer: the immersing happens on the 13th, and on that day nobody can know how many people will end up joining the פסח group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: More people could still register before the slaughter. Then the meat would not be plentiful, and a חגיגה would be needed. So the owner should immerse the cleaver just in case.

keyTerms.meaning: How do they know?

phrases.english: How do they know?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how do they know on the 13th that the offering will be plentiful?

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פסח was plentiful.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whether the meat is plentiful is decided only on the 14th, but the immersing must be done on the 13th, so nobody could rely on it in advance.

steps.title: The offering was brought in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its answer: the פסח was brought בטומאה, and in that case no חגיגה is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is a פסח that came in a state of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer and suggests a new one: the פסח was offered while the community was impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the community is impure, the פסח is still offered בטומאה, but the חגיגה is not. With no חגיגה, the cleaver is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the previous answer is dropped and a new one is offered.
A פסח offered while the community is impure. It is allowed, but the חגיגה is not brought with it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is one that came in impurity.
phrases.notes: A פסח brought in impurity has no accompanying חגיגה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 2 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the case with a different one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plentiful-meat case fails because nobody can know it in advance.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a פסח הבא בטומאה there is no חגיגה, so there is no cleaver.

steps.title: Still, how would they know in advance
steps.stepSummary: The same problem comes back: on the 13th, how would they know the community will be impure on the 14th?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, how do they know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its objection: the new answer has the same weakness as the old one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether the community will be impure is also decided only on the 14th. On the 13th, the community might still turn out to be mostly pure. Then a חגיגה would be needed, and the cleaver should be immersed.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, ultimately. Signals that the same problem still remains.

phrases.english: Ultimately, how do they know?
phrases.notes: How do they know on the 13th that the offering will be brought in impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the objection of step 2 to the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the פסח came בטומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impurity on the 14th cannot be known on the 13th, when the immersing happens.

steps.title: The נשיא died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נשיא died, so everyone will certainly become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the נשיא died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case where the impurity is known for sure: the נשיא has died, and everyone becomes impure by attending his funeral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the נשיא dies, all of Israel becomes impure to honor him at his burial. That makes the impurity of the community certain, which would answer the question 'how do they know?'

keyTerms.meaning: The leader of the generation. When he dies, everyone becomes impure to attend his burial.
Who died.

phrases.english: Where the Nasi died.
phrases.notes: Everyone becomes impure to bury him, so the offering will certainly be brought in impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by supplying a reason why the impurity is known.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impurity cannot be known in advance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death of the נשיא makes everyone impure, so the impurity is known.

steps.title: If he died on the 13th, why immerse the knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the נשיא died. If it was on the 13th, there is no point in immersing even the slaughtering knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נשיא died — when? If you say he died on the 13th, why do I need the knife to be immersed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins testing the new answer by asking which day the נשיא died. Here it rejects the first option, the 13th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the נשיא died on the 13th, everyone is already impure. The knife will become impure again anyway. So immersing the סכין would be pointless, yet the source says it was immersed.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say. Introduces the first option in a 'which one is it?' challenge.
Why do I need it? What is the point?
He immerses it in a מקוה.

phrases.english: The Nasi died — when?
phrases.notes: Sets up a two-sided challenge.

phrases.english: If you say he died on the thirteenth —
why do I need the knife to be immersed?
phrases.notes: Everyone is already impure, so immersing is pointless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5 by asking about the timing of the death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the נשיא died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death on the 13th would make immersing the knife pointless.

steps.title: If he died on the 14th, why treat knife and cleaver differently
steps.stepSummary: If the נשיא died on the 14th, nobody knew about the impurity on the 13th. Then there is no reason to treat the knife and the cleaver differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he died on the 14th. Then what is different about the knife, which he immerses, and what is different about the cleaver, which he does not immerse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second option: a death on the 14th brings back the original problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the 13th, the person had no idea the נשיא would die. Since he did not know, he should prepare for a normal, pure פסח and immerse both tools. So the difference between the knife and the cleaver is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Why treat these two cases differently?
The slaughtering knife, needed for the פסח itself.

phrases.english: Rather, he died on the fourteenth.
What is different about the knife, that he immerses it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קוֹפִיץ דְּלָא מַטְבֵּיל לֵהּ?
phrases.english: and what is different about the cleaver, that he does not immerse it?
phrases.notes: On the 13th he did not know about the impurity, so both tools should be immersed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּמִית בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר. מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second side of the two-sided challenge begun in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the נשיא died, if the death was on the 14th.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without knowing about the death on the 13th, there is no basis for immersing one tool and not the other.

steps.title: The נשיא was dying on the 13th: one doubt versus two doubts
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא was a גוסס on the 13th. The knife involves one doubt, so he immerses it. The cleaver involves two doubts, so he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for a case where the נשיא was dying on the 13th. The knife, which involves one doubt, he immerses. The cleaver, which involves two doubts, he does not immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: on the 13th the נשיא was dying but not yet dead, so everything is uncertain. The number of uncertainties decides which tool to immerse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knife has one doubt: maybe the נשיא will die and everyone will be impure. If he lives, the knife will definitely be needed, so he immerses it. The cleaver has two doubts: maybe the נשיא will die, and even if he lives, maybe the פסח will be plentiful and no חגיגה will be brought. With two reasons it may not be needed, he does not bother to immerse it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... Introduces the specific case where the ruling applies.
A dying person, at the very end of life.
A doubt or uncertainty.
Two doubts.

steps.whatToRemember: The final case is a נשיא who is a גוסס on the 13th. The knife has one doubt (will he die?), so it is immersed. The cleaver has two doubts (will he die? and will there even be a חגיגה?), so it is not immersed. This uses both earlier answers: impurity and plentiful meat.
steps.confusionAlert: The two earlier answers (plentiful meat and impurity) were not thrown away. Here they come back as the two doubts that apply to the cleaver.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one doubt can be enough to require preparing, while two doubts together can make preparing unnecessary.

phrases.aramaic: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּנָשִׂיא גּוֹסֵס בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: It is needed only where the Nasi was dying on the thirteenth.
A knife, which has one doubt — he immerses it.
phrases.notes: The only doubt is whether the נשיא will die. If he lives, the knife is needed.

phrases.aramaic: קוֹפִיץ, דִּתְרֵי סְפֵיקֵי — לָא מַטְבֵּיל לֵהּ.
phrases.english: A cleaver, which has two doubts — he does not immerse it.
phrases.notes: Maybe the נשיא will die, and even if not, maybe the פסח will be plentiful and there will be no חגיגה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּנָשִׂיא גּוֹסֵס בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two-sided challenge of steps 6 and 7 with a third timing: the נשיא was dying, not yet dead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a middle case and counting the doubts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A death on the 13th or the 14th cannot explain why the knife and the cleaver are treated differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the נשיא is a גוסס, the knife involves one doubt and is immersed, while the cleaver involves two doubts and is not.

steps.title: יהודה בן דורתאי breaks away over the חגיגה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that יהודה בן דורתאי and his son left the חכמים and moved to the south. He held that the חגיגה of the 14th overrides שבת, and he was amazed that שמעיה and אבטליון did not teach this.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: יהודה בן דורתאי separated himself, he and his son דורתאי, and went and settled in the south. He said: If אליהו comes and asks the Jewish people, 'Why didn't you bring the חגיגה on שבת?', what will they answer him? I am amazed at the two greatest men of the generation, שמעיה and אבטליון. They are great sages and great expounders of the Torah, yet they did not tell the Jewish people that the חגיגה overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a man who disagreed with the חכמים so strongly that he left. In his view, the חגיגה brought on ערב פסח overrides שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha accepted by the חכמים is that the חגיגה of the 14th does not override שבת. יהודה בן דורתאי held that it does, and he was so sure of this that he separated from the community. He imagines that אליהו will one day ask why the people never brought it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
He separated himself / broke away
The festival שלמים offering brought along with the קרבן פסח
Overrides שבת (may be offered even on שבת)
Expounders of the Torah's פסוקים

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Yehuda ben Dortai separated himself
phrases.notes: He split off from the other חכמים.

phrases.english: he and Dortai his son,
and went and settled in the south.
phrases.notes: He moved far from Jerusalem.

phrases.english: He said: If Elijah comes
and says to the Jewish people:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא חֲגַגְתֶּם חֲגִיגָה בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Why did you not bring the Festival offering on Shabbat,
what will they say to him?
I am amazed at the two greatest men of the generation,
Shemaya and Avtalyon,
who are great sages and great expounders,
and yet they did not tell the Jewish people
that the Festival offering overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the knife-and-cleaver discussion ends, the גמרא brings a ברייתא recording a dissenting view on whether the חגיגה overrides שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה בן דורתאי held that the חגיגה of the 14th overrides שבת, against the accepted view of the חכמים.

steps.title: רב explains the source for בן דורתאי
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that בן דורתאי learned his view from the פסוק 'וזבחת פסח... צאן ובקר'. Since a פסח cannot come from cattle, 'בקר' must refer to the חגיגה, and the Torah calls both of them 'פסח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: What is בן דורתאי's reason? The פסוק says, 'And you shall slaughter the פסח to ה׳ your God, flock and herd.' But a פסח only comes from sheep and goats! So it must mean this: 'flock' is the פסח, and 'herd' is the חגיגה. The Torah calls both of them 'And you shall slaughter the פסח'. So the חגיגה is like the פסח and overrides שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the Torah source behind בן דורתאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions 'בקר' (cattle), but a קרבן פסח is never brought from cattle. So 'בקר' must point to a different קרבן that comes along with the פסח, which is the חגיגה. Because the Torah groups the חגיגה under the word 'פסח', בן דורתאי concludes that it shares the פסח's laws, including overriding שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Flock (sheep and goats) and herd (cattle)
Sheep and goats, the only animals valid for a פסח
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: צאן includes both sheep and goats. Only בקר (cattle) is invalid for a פסח, so the problem in the פסוק is the word 'בקר'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֶן דּוֹרְתַאי,
phrases.english: Rav said: What is the reason of ben Dortai?
As it is written: "And you shall slaughter the Paschal offering to the Lord your God,
flock and herd,"
but doesn't the Paschal offering come only
from the sheep and from the goats?!
Rather: "flock" is the Paschal offering,
"herd" is the Festival offering,
and the Torah says, "And you shall slaughter the Paschal offering" (about both)!
phrases.notes: The חגיגה is therefore treated like the פסח and overrides שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֶן דּוֹרְתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the Torah source for the view quoted in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'בקר' in the פסוק refers to the חגיגה. Since the Torah calls it 'פסח', it shares the פסח's power to override שבת.

steps.title: רב אשי refuses to explain the reasoning of those who broke away
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether we should bother working out the reasoning of people who split from the חכמים. He rejects using the פסוק to support בן דורתאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Should we get up and explain the reasoning of those who separated themselves from the community?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב's explanation. He says there is no need to explain the view of someone who broke away from the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is rhetorical, and the expected answer is 'no'. Because בן דורתאי's view was rejected and he left the community, רב אשי holds that we should not read the פסוק as his source. This sets up step 12, which gives the פסוק a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who separated themselves (here, בן דורתאי and his son)
Shall we get up and explain? (a wordplay on פרוש, 'separated')

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And we, the reasoning of those who separated,
should we get up and explain it?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical question, meaning 'Of course not!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וַאֲנַן טַעְמָא דִּפְרוּשִׁים נֵיקוּ וְנִפְרוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's use of the פסוק as a source for בן דורתאי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's reading of 'צאן ובקר' as the source for בן דורתאי's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no reason to build a Torah source for a view held by people who broke away from the חכמים. The פסוק should be used for an accepted halacha instead.

steps.title: The פסוק is really for רב נחמן's rule about leftover פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the פסוק actually teaches רב נחמן's rule. רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, asks for the source that a leftover פסח (מותר הפסח) is brought as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק comes to teach the view of רב נחמן. For רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: From where do we know that a leftover פסח is offered as a שלמים?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the פסוק a new job. The גמרא is setting up a source question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מותר הפסח is an animal set aside for a פסח that ended up unused, for example one that was lost and found after another animal was brought in its place. רב נחמן's rule is that such an animal is brought as a שלמים. Here the גמרא only asks for the source of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover פסח: an animal (or money) set aside for a פסח that was not used
Peace-offering
From where do we know? (asks for a source)
The פסוק

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא קְרָא לְכִדְרַב נַחְמָן הוּא דַּאֲתָא,
phrases.english: Rather, the verse comes for the teaching of Rav Naḥman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: for Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
From where do we know that a leftover Paschal offering
is offered as a peace-offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קְרָא לְכִדְרַב נַחְמָן הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב's reading, רב אשי assigns the פסוק to a different, accepted halacha.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.

steps.title: 'צאן ובקר' teaches that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The source is the same פסוק. Since a פסח cannot come from cattle, 'צאן ובקר' teaches that a leftover פסח is used for a קרבן that can come from both flock and herd, which is a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'And you shall slaughter the פסח to ה׳ your God, flock and herd.' Does a פסח come from cattle? Doesn't a פסח come only from sheep and goats? Rather, it teaches that a leftover פסח should be used for something that comes from flock and from herd, meaning a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נחמן's question with the same 'צאן ובקר' פסוק, now read in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty is the same as before: a פסח cannot come from בקר. רב נחמן solves it differently. The פסוק is describing what happens to a leftover פסח: it is brought as a קרבן that may come from both צאן and בקר. That קרבן is a שלמים, not a חגיגה that overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so? (introduces a rhetorical challenge)

keyTerms.term: לְדָבָר הַבָּא מִן הַצֹּאן וּמִן הַבָּקָר
keyTerms.meaning: For something that comes from flock and herd, meaning a שלמים

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, 'צאן ובקר', is read in two ways. בן דורתאי's way (explained by רב) is that the חגיגה is like the פסח and overrides שבת. רב אשי rejects that and uses רב נחמן's way: a leftover פסח is brought as a שלמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the accepted halacha of מותר הפסח its Torah source. It also explains the extra word 'בקר' without supporting the rejected view that the חגיגה overrides שבת.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר״.
phrases.english: As it is stated: "And you shall slaughter the Paschal offering to the Lord your God, flock and herd."
Does a Paschal offering come from the herd?
Doesn't a Paschal offering come only
from the sheep and from the goats?!
Rather, a leftover Paschal offering shall be for something
that comes from the flock and from the herd.
phrases.notes: That is, a שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְזָבַחְתָּ פֶּסַח לַה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ צֹאן וּבָקָר״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בקר' in the פסוק cannot describe a פסח itself. So it teaches that a leftover פסח becomes a קרבן that can come from flock or herd, which is a שלמים.

steps.title: Why don't the רבנן let the חגיגה override שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the רבנן, who say the חגיגה does not override שבת, even though it looks like a קרבן ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, why does it not override שבת? It is surely a communal offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who disagree with בן דורתאי. It challenges them: why would the חגיגה not override שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן ציבור, an offering of the whole community, normally overrides שבת. The חגיגה is brought by the entire nation at the same time, so it seems to belong in that group. The question is: what stops it from overriding שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view)
What is the reason?
Overrides שבת
A communal offering, which normally overrides שבת

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is the reason
that it does not override Shabbat?
phrases.notes: Refers to the חגיגה.

phrases.english: It is certainly a communal offering!
phrases.notes: Since everyone brings it at the same time, it seems like a public offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא דָּחֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בן דורתאי's view (which was rejected) to the reasoning of the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's position that the חגיגה does not override שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חגיגה is like a קרבן ציבור, and a קרבן ציבור overrides שבת. So why shouldn't the חגיגה?

steps.title: The verse says seven days, not eight
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא, quoting רבי יהודה בן ספרא, learns from 'וחגותם אותו... שבעת ימים' that the חגיגה does not override שבת. The festival really has eight days, but one of them is always a שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי יהודה בן ספרא: The פסוק says, 'And you shall celebrate it as a festival to ה׳, seven days in the year.' Seven? There are eight! Rather, from here we learn that the חגיגה does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא gives the source for the רבנן from a פסוק about סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חגיגה can be brought on all eight days, counting שמיני עצרת. Yet the פסוק says 'seven days' for bringing the חגיגה ('וחגותם'). Any eight days in a row always include one שבת. So the Torah is telling us that you can bring it on only seven of them, because it is not brought on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall celebrate,' understood here as bringing the חגיגה
Seven
There are eight
From here (we learn)

steps.confusionAlert: The eighth day is שמיני עצרת. A person can still make up the חגיגה on that day. That is why the count is eight and not seven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the רבנן's rule that the חגיגה does not override שבת, in contrast to בן דורתאי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Safra:
The verse says:
"And you shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord
seven days in the year."
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:מא

phrases.english: Seven? There are eight!
phrases.notes: Including שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: Rather, from here we learn that the festival offering
does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן סָפְרָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by giving a פסוק as the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חגיגה is like a קרבן ציבור and should override שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah says 'seven days' out of eight. This shows that one day, the שבת, is excluded, so the חגיגה does not override שבת.

steps.title: רבין: sometimes there are only six days
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that he challenged his teachers. When the first day of סוכות falls on שבת, only six days are left for the חגיגה, not seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: I said before my teachers: Sometimes you find only six, for example when the first יום טוב of the festival falls on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבין raises a problem with רבי אילעא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first day of סוכות is on שבת, then the eighth day (שמיני עצרת) is also on שבת. Then two of the eight days are lost, and only six remain. So how can the פסוק's 'seven' prove anything exact?

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Before my teachers
Six

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
I said before my teachers:

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה,
phrases.english: There are times when you find only six,
for example, when the first festival day
of the festival falls on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: Then the eighth day is also שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר: אָמַרְתִּי לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from 'seven days' in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the count can be six, then 'seven' is not an exact count. So it may not prove that שבת is excluded.

steps.title: אביי: seven is the usual case, eight never happens
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבין's question. Eight days without a שבת is impossible, while seven days is what happens in most years.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Would the bereaved אבין say such a thing? Eight you never find at all; seven exist in most years.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אילעא's proof and pushes away רבין's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not have to fit every single year. It only has to rule out 'eight', which is impossible if the חגיגה does not override שבת. Seven usable days is the normal situation, so the Torah speaks of seven.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The bereaved אבין' (another name for רבין); a sharp expression of surprise
You never find it at all
Most years

steps.whatToRemember: The 'seven days' of the פסוק shows that the חגיגה does not override שבת. Eight days always include a שבת, and seven usable days is the normal case.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אָבִין תַּכָּלָא לֵימָא כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא?
phrases.english: Would the bereaved Avin say such a thing?
Eight you do not find at all;
seven exist in most years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: אָבִין תַּכָּלָא לֵימָא כִּי הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבין's challenge and keeps the proof from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse describes the normal case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because only six days are sometimes available, the word 'seven' proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eight days with no שבת is impossible. Seven usable days happens in most years, so the פסוק's 'seven' still teaches that the חגיגה does not override שבת.

steps.title: Peace offerings slaughtered before the festival do not count
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports in the name of רבי אלעזר: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not count for the מצוה of שמחה or the מצוה of חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: שלמים that one slaughtered on ערב יום טוב, one does not fulfill with them the מצוה of שמחה, nor the מצוה of חגיגה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי אלעזר about when the festival שלמים must be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different מצוות on the festival can be done with שלמים: שמחה and חגיגה. רבי אלעזר says that if the animal was slaughtered before יום טוב, neither מצוה is fulfilled with it. The גמרא will now give the source for each part.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before the festival
He does not fulfill his obligation
The מצוה of rejoicing with festival offerings

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Peace offerings that one slaughtered on the eve of the festival,
one does not fulfill with them

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִשּׁוּם שִׂמְחָה וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם חֲגִיגָה.
phrases.english: neither the obligation of rejoicing nor that of the festival offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the timing of festival שלמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב count neither for שמחה nor for חגיגה.

steps.title: Source for rejoicing: slaughter must be at the time of rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the source for the שמחה part. The פסוק 'וזבחת... ושמחת' links the slaughtering to the rejoicing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for שמחה (it does not count), as it is written: 'And you shall slaughter... and you shall rejoice.' We require slaughtering (the sentence continues on the next amud: at the time of rejoicing).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving the first half of רבי אלעזר's rule. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts slaughtering and rejoicing side by side. This teaches that the slaughtering must happen during the time of rejoicing, which is יום טוב. An animal slaughtered on ערב יום טוב was not slaughtered then, so it cannot count for שמחה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
And you shall slaughter
We require slaughtering (at a specific time)

phrases.english: As for rejoicing, [it does not count], as it is written:
"And you shall slaughter... and you shall rejoice" —
phrases.notes: דברים כז:ז

phrases.english: we require that the slaughter be
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: 'at the time of rejoicing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the שמחה half of רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.raayaObject: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not count for שמחה
